## Snow Covered Area

Snow Covered Area (SCA) maps delineate the extent of the snowpack, identifying which areas of the terrain are covered by snow and which are snow-free. Each pixel is classified as 0 (snow free) or 1 (snow covered). This binary mask is obtained by thresholding Earth Observation-derived snow maps from the Copernicus Land Monitoring Service (CLMS). The SCA is further used as an assimilation dataset for a correction loop in the GEOtop physical model to adjust the snow line, and thus the minimum snow cover elevation. This layer is a demonstration subset of Waterjade's snow products over Tyrol. It builds on the snow-modelling work first developed within the Digital Twin of the Alps (DTA).
